Subject: ACME - Context length & token volume (pricing follow-up)

Hi Alex / Samira —

Great to meet earlier — thanks for the time. Quick recap and the follow-up items we discussed on the call: 

1) Use cases and targets
- Primary: customer support summarization + guided agent assist (short prompts, long completions).
- Secondary: monthly digest generation for enterprise accounts (longer context).

2) Context length profile (what you shared on the call)
- Avg prompt tokens: ~150 tokens
- Avg completion tokens: ~1,100 tokens
- Percent breakdown by max context need: ~70% of calls fit within 8k, ~25% need 32k, ~5% will require 128k for large digests/enterprise exports.

3) Expected volumes (ballpark ask)
- Target: ~100M tokens / month total (prompts ~15M, completions ~85M).
- Peak patterns: heavy end-of-day digest generation spikes; concurrency needs for agent assist during business hours.

4) Budget & unit economics
- You mentioned target pricing in the $15–$25 per 1M tokens range; also flagged an internal max target of $18/1M for high-volume baseline.
- Looking for committed unit economics and breakout for 8k / 32k / 128k contexts.

Next steps (what I’ll send by EOD):
- A prioritized pricing sheet with tiered/unit rates by context length (8k/32k/128k) and example cost calc for your 100M tokens.
- Sample usage profile template for you to fill (so our cost estimates match your real distribution).
- Proposal for a short pilot: 30-day Dedicated trial with usage cap + reporting.

Attachments: I’m attaching a baseline pricing sheet and a sample usage CSV so you can drop real numbers in.

If any numbers above are off, flag them and I’ll update the model.

Best,
Marissa Cole
Account Executive, Redwood Inference
marissa.cole@redwood.ai | (415) 555-0123

Thanks Marissa — this looks right on the high level. A couple clarifications from our side: 

- The 100M tokens/month is our near-term target (Q3 pilot -> Q4 ramp). We might see 150–200M in 12 months if the pilot goes well.
- The 5% 128k estimate is specifically for our monthly export/digest feature for enterprise customers (about ~1,500 exports/month). All other heavy workloads are 32k or below.
- Our procurement target is to keep baseline unit spend around $15–$18/1M tokens; for the pilot we can accept slightly higher (up to $25/1M) while we validate quality and reliability.

Can you include a worked example of committed vs on-demand pricing and the resulting monthly cost for 100M and 200M token volumes? Also please show incremental cost if 10% of traffic shifts from 8k to 32k.

Thanks — Alex

From: Jordan Blake <jordan.blake@redwood.ai>

Subject: Re: ACME - Context length & token volume (pricing follow-up)

Alex — looping in a quick worked example and proposed tiering so we’re all aligned.

Assumptions (from Marissa / your notes):
- Avg prompt: 150 tokens; avg completion: 1,100 tokens → ~1,250 tokens per request.
- Breakdown: 70% 8k, 25% 32k, 5% 128k.
- Baseline target: 100M tokens / month (prompts + completions combined).

Proposed unit rates (example pricing for pilot):
- 8k-context model: $20 / 1M tokens
- 32k-context model: $32 / 1M tokens
- 128k-context model: $60 / 1M tokens

Worked examples (rounded):
1) 100M tokens/month (70/25/5 split)
- 8k portion (70M tokens) @ $20/1M = $1,400/month
- 32k portion (25M tokens) @ $32/1M = $800/month
- 128k portion (5M tokens) @ $60/1M = $300/month
Total = $2,500/month (~$25/1M effective)

2) 200M tokens/month (same split)
- 8k: 140M @ $20 = $2,800
- 32k: 50M @ $32 = $1,600
- 128k: 10M @ $60 = $600
Total = $5,000/month (~$25/1M effective)

Incremental sensitivity: if 10% of 8k traffic shifts to 32k (moving 10% of 70% => 7% of total), effective cost increases ~6–8% on the above examples. We can provide a small spreadsheet so you can tweak these inputs.

Commit vs On-demand note:
- Committed monthly spend (12-month) can reduce the above unit rates by 15–25% depending on commit level and SLAs (we can model that once you give a target commit).
- On-demand pricing would be ~10–20% higher than the pilot tiers above, with no minimum.

I’ll attach a spreadsheet with line-item math. If $2,500/month for 100M looks off relative to your targets, tell us the target effective $/1M you need and we’ll back into a commit proposal.

-Jordan
